name: Sex hormone-binding globulin
rangeNote: Typical values differ by sex, age and assay, and labs often print age-specific ranges. No population range is built in; use your lab's printed range. SHBG can only be converted between mass and molar units approximately, so only nmol/L is supported.
summary: SHBG (sex hormone-binding globulin) is a protein made mainly by the liver that carries testosterone and estradiol in the blood. It controls how much of these hormones is free to act, so it helps in reading total testosterone.

high.meaning: A higher SHBG holds more testosterone bound, so total testosterone can look normal or high while the free amount is lower. SHBG is raised by estrogens and an overactive thyroid, among other things.
commonCauses: Oral estrogens, oral contraceptive pills and some menopausal hormone treatments
Liver conditions, such as hepatitis or cirrhosis
Low food intake or low body weight

low.meaning: A lower SHBG holds less testosterone bound, so total testosterone can be low while the free amount is closer to normal. Low SHBG is commonly seen with excess body weight and insulin resistance and is linked in studies to type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome, though this does not show it is the cause.
commonCauses: Insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes or metabolic syndrome
Androgens, including testosterone treatment and anabolic steroids
Nephrotic syndrome (protein loss through the kidneys)
